newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up on Thai move towards IMF.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up on Thai move towards IMF.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen gaining on Monday as the government moved closer to involving the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in the management of the ailing economy, analysts said.

After a weekend meeting with IMF officials, government ministers said Thailand was seeking IMF help. The SET Index added 12.58 points to close at 646.58 on Friday. The SET 50 added 1.12 points to 48.80.
"I think it's very positive but it is nothing the market hasn't already expected," said Nimit Wongjariakul, senior vice president at Thaimex Finance and Securities.

"I think it will be good in the long term, in the short term speculative pressure might drive the market up a bit. I don't know when they will officially announce the IMF is coming in. We are just moving a step closer," said Nimit.
Investor expectations the IMF would be asked to help manage the ailing economy have helped support share prices since the baht's de facto devaluation on July 2.
Water supplier East Water is expected to post a strong debut. The firm's 30 baht per share initial offering prior to the baht float was heavily oversubscribed.
